رَجْرَاجٌ : see رَجْرَجٌ. ―
-b2- [Hence,] رَجْرَاجَةٌ A woman, (S,) or girl, (A,) whose flesh, (S,) or hinder part, (A,) quivers, or quakes; (S, A;) [and so ↓ مُتَرَجْرِجَةٌ , occurring in the A and TA in art. ديص.] ―
-b3- And ثَرِيدَةٌ رَجْرَاجَةٌ: see رِجْرِجٌ. ―
-b4- And كَتِيبَةٌ رَجْرَاجَةٌ (tropical:) And army, or a troop, agitated to and fro (A, L) in its march, (L,) scarcely moving onwards, (A, L,) by reason of its multitude: (L:) or as though agitated to and fro, and not moving onwards, by reason of its multitude. (S.) ―
-b5- See also رَجَاجٌ. ―
-b6- Also A certain medicine, (L, K,) well known. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
